Diurnal heating under strong August insolation typically drives rapid afternoon rises, but even modest increases in boundary-layer moisture, subtle cloud development, or shifts in wind direction can trim the peak by a degree. Measurement at the official Incheon station (versus urban Seoul sites) further amplifies sensitivity to these local factors.

**Historical August averages near 30–31°C provide context, yet current model consensus and real-time observations keep probabilities tightly balanced.** Any late-day sea breeze strengthening or minor radiative cooling could favor 31°C resolution, while sustained clear conditions and peak solar heating support 32°C. The low odds on 33°C or higher underscore the limited upside once the heatwave influence wanes.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent southwest monsoon conditions are keeping the highest temperature in Manila on August 12 firmly positioned around 30°C.** Official PAGASA forecasts project a maximum of 30°C (with 90% rain chance) for Metro Manila, citing widespread cloud cover and precipitation that suppress daytime heating. This aligns with the long-term August climatology of ~31°C highs, but current monsoon-driven moisture and cloudiness are capping readings at the lower end of the typical 30–33°C range.

Recent model consensus and station observations show limited solar insolation due to overcast skies and frequent showers, reducing the likelihood of brief clearing that could push temps to 31–32°C. Higher thresholds (33°C+) remain improbable without a ridge or subsidence event, which is absent in the current pattern. Traders have therefore concentrated probability on the 30°C outcome, reflecting the strong consensus from authoritative forecasts that widespread rain and high humidity will constrain the daily peak.

**Marine layer depth and onshore flow are the dominant factors shaping trader consensus around a 66-67°F high for San Francisco on August 13.** Official National Weather Service and AccuWeather guidance point to a persistent marine layer keeping coastal areas under clouds or overcast skies, limiting daytime heating to the mid-to-upper 60s at KSFO and downtown stations. This aligns closely with the market-implied odds, where 66-67°F leads at 36.5% and 68-69°F follows at 27.5%, reflecting modest uncertainty in exact clearing timing or layer thickness.

Recent model runs show a cooling trend through mid-August, with sea breezes strengthening and preventing significant inland warmth from reaching the immediate coast. Historical August averages near 69°F provide context, but current conditions favor the lower end of the normal range due to enhanced onshore flow and possible light drizzle overnight. Traders appear to weigh these dynamics against slight model spread on afternoon sun exposure, which could nudge readings into the upper 60s if the layer thins earlier than expected. No major synoptic shifts are anticipated before resolution, keeping focus on the 64-69°F band where most probability is concentrated.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by the Hong Kong Observatory in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the Hong Kong Observatory, specifically the "Absolute Daily Max (deg. C)" the specified date once information is finalized in the relevant "Daily Extract", available here: https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/cis/climat.htm

This market can not resolve until data for this date has been published.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures in Celsius to one decimal place (eg, 9.1°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is initially published for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.
